title: Make land --pr rerun a failed check once and name the failing test
summary: `athena land --pr` already polls checks for about ten minutes (30 looks, 20 s apart), but a red check ends the run with no retry and no detail. I read the request as: keep the bounded wait, rerun the failed check jobs once when a check fails and wait again, and on a second failure report the failing test's name. The audience is the operator who wants a landing to finish unattended.

defaults_applied.how: New unit tests with fake host; cargo test and clippy must be clean.
Criteria check the rerun and the failing-test report happening, via fake-host tests.
The retry sits inside land_pr's check wait, not as a caller-side wrapper.
One focused change in the gh.rs landing flow plus its display.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Waiting already exists (Poll, 30 x 20 s); that bound is kept, applied to the first wait and to the rerun wait separately or in total, and stated in the code.
Only failed check jobs are re-run (GitHub rerun-failed-jobs), once per land invocation; a stored count is not needed beyond the invocation unless the design needs it.
The failing test's name is extracted from the failed job's log or annotations for cargo test output (`test x::y ... FAILED`); if none is found the report says so rather than guessing.
The merge gate is unchanged: nothing merges unless the checks are green and merge_via_rest is on.
Exit code stays 2 unless the checks end green or the job lands.

acceptance_criteria.text: A unit test in gh.rs with a fake PrHost shows a first red check triggers exactly one rerun of the failed jobs, then a second wait; if the rerun goes green, land_pr reports Green and merges when merge_via_rest is on. Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`.
A unit test shows a second red result triggers no further rerun and the PrReport carries the failing test's name (parsed from the failed job's log or annotations). Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`.

A test shows that checks still pending after the bounded number of looks make land_pr return Pending without rerunning or merging, and that the total wait across the first wait, the rerun and the second wait stays bounded.
The text printed by display::land_pr names the failing test on a second failure and says that the failed job was re-run once. The JSON report includes the same field.

The real GhClient implements the rerun through the GitHub rerun-failed-jobs endpoint and reads the failing test name from a real host reply shape. This is covered by a parser test on a sample payload. Any new host calls go through the existing HostOperation retry and redaction path.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` all pass with no warnings.
The design doc or CHANGELOG states the new behavior (wait, one rerun, failing-test report) so a stranger can find it.

out_of_scope: Changing the merge gate or the merge_via_rest setting
Rerunning more than once or rerunning passing jobs
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass odds than the reference. The change adds a new host call, log parsing and a second wait loop to a large gh.rs, and the failing-test extraction format is uncertain.
